header.userPrompt:
Add duplicate-expense detection to the expenses page plus a backend merge operation, so the user can find and collapse expenses that represent the same purchase (one linked to a bank statement row, the other linked to a receipt).

## Background: the real problem
The user imported two years of CARREFOUR receipts (each became an expense linked to its receipt) AFTER importing "Ready" bank statement rows that rules had matched to CARREFOUR (each became an expense linked to its row). The result is duplicate expense pairs: for one real purchase there are now two expenses, one carrying the bank statement row, the other carrying the receipt. They want to detect such pairs and merge each into a single expense that keeps the row and gains the receipt. This is a one-time-shaped cleanup but must generalize to any merchant, not just CARREFOUR.

Note: the recently shipped Ready-tab receipt auto-match only attaches receipts that are still UNLINKED at process time. These duplicates already both became expenses, so that feature does not fix them. This is a separate detect-and-merge flow.

## Scope decision: phase 1, frontend detection + backend merge, NO persistence
- Detection runs in the frontend. The expenses page already loads all expenses; compute duplicate candidates client-side. Do NOT add a detection endpoint, a suggestions table, or any persisted "dismiss/ignore" state in this phase. Dismissing a suggestion is in-memory only (it reappears on reload); this is intentional so we can first measure how many real duplicates and how many false candidates exist before deciding whether a persisted inbox is worth building. Do not build that inbox now.
- Merge runs in the backend as one transaction (details below).

## Detection (frontend, pure + unit-tested)
Add a pure function (natural home: a new object under `net.wiringbits.utils` or alongside the expenses-page logic, matching how other pages keep pure logic in a `*Logic`/util object) that takes the loaded expenses and returns duplicate candidates. A candidate is a PAIR of two expenses where:
- exactly one of the two has a bank_statement_row linked and the other has NO row linked (survivor = the row-linked one, loser = the no-row one);
- the two amounts are equal (exact, same currency/sign handling as the rest of the app; do not fabricate or coerce);
- the two dates are equal, or within the same small day window already used by the matcher (reuse `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays` rather than a new constant). A missing date is never a match.

Tier the candidates by confidence:
- STRONG: amount + date + MERCHANT all match (same merchant id). High confidence, one-click merge.
- WEAK: amount + date match but MERCHANT differs. Lower confidence, shown separately, user must view the receipt to compare before merging.

Explicit exclusions (must be unit-tested):
- two expenses with the same amount+date(+merchant) but BOTH linked to rows (to different rows) are NOT candidates, they are two real transactions;
- a pair where NEITHER has a row is out of scope (no row-survivor), not a candidate;
- a missing date on either side is never a candidate.

## Merge (backend, one transaction)
New action + endpoint to merge a loser expense into a survivor expense, both owned by the authenticated user (user-scoped checks on every query). Given survivorId and loserId:
1. validate both belong to the user and that the survivor has a row linked and the loser does not (reject otherwise, loud error, no silent no-op);
2. repoint the loser's receipt link to the survivor (reuse the existing receipt link path / `receiptRepository.linkToExpense` and its unlinked-only guard semantics; the survivor must not already have a receipt, else fail loudly);
3. repoint any `refund` rows that reference the loser (`refund.expense_id`) to the survivor. This matters: `refund.expense_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a plain delete would silently orphan a refund. Carry it over instead;
4. delete the loser expense. Its `expense_category_split` rows are `ON DELETE CASCADE` and go away with it (the survivor keeps its own splits, which is the intended outcome);
5. all of the above in a single DB transaction.

Confirm against the schema (evolutions) that these are the only FKs referencing `expense(id)`: `expense_category_split` (CASCADE), `bank_statement_row.expense_id` (SET NULL), `receipt.expense_id` (SET NULL), `refund.expense_id` (SET NULL). If a new reference exists, handle it; do not leave a silently-nulled reference.

The survivor keeps its own amount, date, merchant, category, splits, and row link. The loser contributes only its receipt (and any refund). The merge never changes the survivor's own fields.

## UI (expenses page)
- Surface duplicate candidates on the expenses page (a section, tab, or panel consistent with the existing page structure). Show STRONG and WEAK groups separately.
- Each candidate shows the two expenses side by side: amount, date, merchant, category, which side has the row vs the receipt, so the user can compare.
- Provide a way to VIEW the receipt to compare before merging. Reuse the existing shared receipt-file viewer helper `net.wiringbits.utils.ReceiptFileViewer` (added in the previous PR, opens the receipt file in a new tab). Do NOT duplicate blob/Uint8Array open logic and do NOT build a new modal.
- The user decides per pair: "Merge" (calls the backend merge, survivor = the row-linked expense) or "Dismiss" (in-memory hide for this session only; no persistence).
- After a successful merge, update the page state in place (the loser disappears, the survivor now shows the receipt) following the existing page-scoped state pattern; do not force a full remount/refetch if the page already avoids that.

## Rules and constraints
- Merge is destructive (deletes an expense). It is always explicit per pair and user-confirmed. Never auto-merge, never bulk-merge in this phase.
- Survivor is ALWAYS the row-linked expense; loser is ALWAYS the no-row expense. Reject any merge request that does not fit this shape.
- No silent bad data: exact amount match, never a fabricated date, fail loudly on any guard violation (loser has no receipt, survivor already has a receipt, either not owned by user, wrong row/no-row shape).
- All DB queries user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?); list queries have a stable ORDER BY.
- No DB CHECK constraints for business rules; app-level validation.
- Follow `docs/guide/frontend.md` and `docs/guide/testing.md`. Test descriptions name a single method (no type prefix), per `.orca/reviewers/tests.md`.
- Match existing code style; surgical changes only.

## Tests
- Frontend detection: unit-test STRONG vs WEAK tiering, exact-amount requirement, date-window boundaries (0, MaxDateDifferenceDays, just outside), missing-date excluded, both-rows excluded, neither-row excluded, correct survivor/loser assignment.
- Backend merge: receipt relinked to survivor, refund rows repointed to survivor, loser deleted, loser's splits gone, survivor's own fields unchanged, all in one transaction; guard failures (not owned, wrong shape, survivor already has a receipt) rejected. Follow the existing action/repository test patterns.
- Full suite must pass as CI runs it.

## Out of scope (do NOT build now)
- No persisted suggestions/inbox table, no persisted dismiss/ignore state.
- No detection endpoint (detection is frontend-only).
- No auto-merge or bulk-merge.
- No changes to the Ready-tab receipt auto-match, the Auto-Reconcile page, or `ReconciliationMatcher.reconcile`.
- No new receipt-view modal (reuse `ReceiptFileViewer`).
- No change to how receipts or rows are parsed, imported, or confirmed.
